  "text": "The man at the repair counter set Daniel's radio on a square of felt.

“It works,” he said.

“It cuts out after a while.”

“How long?”

“Depends.”

The man plugged it in. A woman was reading the weather. Rain would reach the coast by evening.

Daniel rested his shopping bag against the counter.

“I can leave it with you.”

“We've got a three-week wait.”

“That's all right.”

The man turned the dial. Music came through, then a discussion about parking charges.

“Does it happen on every station?”

“I only use the one.”

He brought the dial back slowly until the weather returned.

“There?”

“A little further.”

The man adjusted it.

Daniel nodded.

A strip of brown tape crossed the battery cover. His father had written their surname on it before taking the radio into hospital. Daniel had tried lifting one corner, but the plastic underneath was a different colour.

“Could be the power lead,” the man said.

“Can you replace that?”

“Probably. They don't make this connector anymore.”

He moved the lead where it entered the casing. The woman's voice disappeared.

“There,” Daniel said.

The man held it still. They waited. When he let go, the voice came back.

“I'll need your number.”

Daniel gave it to him. The man wrote it on a ticket and pushed the copy across.

“Keep that somewhere safe.”

Daniel put it in his wallet, behind his father's library card.

At the door, he remembered his shopping. The man had already lifted the bag onto the counter, clear of the tools."
